executive_preview: The strongest signal this week is strategic tension between electrification ambitions and market, regulatory and supply-chain constraints. Automakers continue expanding EV capability, charging infrastructure, software and autonomous mobility, but adoption evidence remains uneven: Toyota's broader EV lineup lifted U.S. EV sales, while Volvo canceled the EX40 amid falling sales and a CLEPA survey found only 8% of respondents in five major European markets intend to buy an EV next.

lead_development.title: Capability and nostalgia are being used to defend differentiation in a converging vehicle market.
lead_development.what_happened: Honda is making TrailSport genuinely more capable, Toyota continues to sell hybrid off-road SUVs despite modest fuel economy, and Mercedes-AMG is reviving a highly exclusive V8 sports coupe. Collector and custom-car coverage also remains strong, including licensed Eleanor builds and Porsche safari conversions.
lead_development.why_it_matters: Automakers are using distinct experiences—off-road utility, mechanical performance and heritage—to justify premium positioning in markets where many vehicles increasingly share platforms and software. This may support margin, but specialized products have limited volume and should not be mistaken for broad-market demand.

signals.title: U.S. Scrutiny of Chinese Automotive Partnerships Raises Strategic and Compliance Risk
signals.teaser: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy criticized Ford's relationships with CATL, Geely and BYD, with particular attention to CATL technology licensed for Ford's Michigan battery plant and Ford's planned continued production of the Lincoln Nautilus in China.

signals.title: EV Adoption Is Becoming More Product- and Market-Specific
Automakers Are Expanding Capability-Focused Products Rather Than Abandoning Utility Segments
signals.teaser: Honda substantially reworked the 2027 Passport TrailSport, increasing ground clearance to 9.65 inches and redesigning nearly 70% of major suspension components.

downside.title: Policy restrictions on Chinese technology could disrupt battery, software and vehicle sourcing plans.
downside.teaser: Ford's CATL and Geely relationships are already drawing public government criticism, while China retains dominant positions in battery processing and exports.

upside.title: Use independent EV battery diagnostics to improve used-EV pricing and customer confidence.
upside.teaser: AVILOO is expanding its battery warranty across Europe because manufacturer-reported battery health is not standardized or independently verified.
